decisions.summary: make land returns at once, with refusal and cure, when the claims refusal is an INTRODUCED finding / known drift / anything only an edit or ruling cures
decisions.why: Exactly FR-001 and the approved fix 1 ('stop waiting when the claims gate refuses for a reason waiting can't fix').

decisions.summary: the fast exit fires only when the refusal names NO 'owed (' line, so a refusal carrying an introduced finding AND an owed claim still waits the full round
decisions.why: No in-flight check can cure the introduced part, so the land refuses after the wait anyway: that is FR-001's case literally ('MUST NOT wait ... when the refusal is one no in-flight check can cure') and the GM's 'a reason waiting can't fix'. Not impossible, not implied by the request, and it keeps the 20-minute waste the fix exists to remove. Should say: fail fast whenever any part of the refusal cannot be cured by waiting, listing the owed claims beside the rest.

decisions.summary: an 'owed (' refusal is treated as 'a check may be in flight' and keeps today's wait, because no registry of in-flight claims checks exists
decisions.why: FR-002 and SC-002 key on whether a check IS in flight ('refuses with nothing in flight never enters the claims wait'); the plan substitutes 'the gate says owed', so an owed claim nobody dispatched still waits 20 minutes, a reason waiting can't fix. The stated reason (no registry exists) is an implementation-cost argument, not impossibility: a marker written when a claims check is dispatched/started would make in-flight observable. Should say: wait only while an in-flight check is observable (e.g. such a marker), or take this narrowing to the GM via the arbiter.

decisions.summary: one docstring-blind code id in pipeline/codeid.py (drop module/class/function docstrings and constant-claim strings, dump AST without attributes, hash); gate-stamp calls it; unparsable files hashed by bytes
decisions.why: FR-003/FR-004 and the GM's 'omitting docstrings when hashing code'; one copy of the rule serves the audit.

decisions.summary: gencache._split_sources and render_cache.engine_fingerprint key on codeid
interactive/** (class docstrings are modal text via cls.__doc__) stays hashed by bytes in the roll and render keys, the rule and reason at the point of change
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own words ('failing to strip docstrings when we SHOULD') and carried by FR-004/FR-005's content exception: a docstring that is the artifact's content, hashed blind, would serve a stale render, defeating the cache exactness the request presumes (SC-006). Page assets are not docstrings at all.

decisions.summary: gate-stamp content_id (RAW_AREAS raw), ci/delta engine_key, cohort_known engine_key kept as they are
decisions.why: Already docstring-blind; RAW_AREAS is the existing content exception FR-004 allows.

decisions.summary: ci/state.py tooling_hash moves .py to codeid except each file's MODULE docstring (scripts print it as usage); Makefile and non-.py raw
decisions.why: A content exception under FR-004: a module docstring printed as usage is output the tooling tests can observe. Note, not blocking: the row says today's raw hashing is 'deliberately' so and the plan does not record what that reason was; if the tooling tests read function docstrings too, stripping them serves a stale pass, an FR-004 content case the audit would have missed. Record the reason in research.md and at the point of change.

decisions.summary: ci/gate_config config_hash and record_cache code_sha move .py to codeid; lockfiles/config raw
decisions.why: FR-004: places that fail to strip docstrings when they should, fixed.

decisions.summary: record_build fingerprint kept raw (the built site reads research claims from docstrings); claims fingerprints kept (the claim text is what is checked)
decisions.why: FR-004's own exception: the docstring is content of what the site produces; the GM's 'when we should' implies such sites exist. The claims case is the spec's edge case.

decisions.summary: plan_*, hm_*, record/* other hashes are text, not code: no change
decisions.why: Not code-staleness keys; FR-004 covers code-hashing sites.

decisions.summary: cohort_audit --failed-first/--last-failed/--exitfirst; last run = newest same-block record of this clone, none -> say so and roll all; ordered_specs and roll_until_failure; early stop cancels unstarted, lets started finish, exit 1
decisions.why: FR-007 and the GM's pytest-style modes; letting started seeds finish is pytest-xdist -x behavior in a parallel pool.

decisions.summary: --last-failed/--exitfirst runs write records marked partial, refused by cohort_gate.landing_shaped; cohort-landing passes none of the modes
decisions.why: Enforces FR-008.

decisions.summary: LAST_FAILED reads only the newest record's failing seeds, so failures an EXITFIRST partial run did not roll are forgotten
decisions.why: Full run fails 3, 7, 9; LAST_FAILED=1 EXITFIRST=1 rolls 3, fails, stops - the record says failing {3}; the next LAST_FAILED=1 rolls only 3; once fixed it reports nothing failing, and 7 and 9 reappear only at the landing - the wasted round the GM is cutting. The GM asked for 'the pytest thing'; pytest's lastfailed keeps unrun failures until they pass. Should say: a partial record carries forward the failures of the run it selected from that it did not roll.

decisions.summary: every run prints 'rolled N, served M'
decisions.why: The measurement that enforces SC-001/FR-012; verification of what was asked.

decisions.summary: FR-012 'holds by D3' and is pinned by a test that runs a cohort twice at one code and asserts zero rolled
decisions.why: FR-012 names its test: 'a landing right after a full cohort run at the same code rolls no seed', and the GM's own example is 'run the seeds locally and then do a make landing'. Two cohort runs never exercise the landing path (its worktree, environment and seed block), so 'holds by D3' is a premise the substituted test cannot measure. Should say: the test runs a full cohort, then make cohort-landing (the land path), and asserts zero rolled.

decisions.summary: make probe [WT=] [EXITFIRST=1] runs the landing cohort, HEAD's fresh block and make map for each live hamlet; HEAD's verdicts stored per engine key and block under .git/probe-baselines, rolled once in a detached worktree when absent; EXITFIRST stops at the first seed worse than HEAD's
decisions.why: FR-009, SC-003, SC-004, approved fix 2.

decisions.summary: the probe prints only seeds whose verdict differs from HEAD's
decisions.why: Approved fix 2: 'print each seed's result and each changed field against HEAD'; FR-009: 'per-seed verdict comparisons'. A seed failing the same way at HEAD and in the probe - the seed being iterated on - would be invisible. Should say: print every seed's verdict against HEAD's, differences marked (the field changes may stay changed-only, as the fix's words say).

decisions.summary: task-add writes a section with the alone-off table header and item 6's D35 red exit wording; a SECTION= file whose item 6 lacks make arbiter-ask gets a warning and is filed
decisions.why: FR-010 and approved fix 3.

decisions.summary: Summary, Technical Context (probe-baseline store, reference roll first), Performance bookends, Constitution Check, Project Structure, Complexity Tracking
decisions.why: Restate the spec or lay out the files for decisions above; none decide anything the spec left open beyond them.

decisions.id: Summary: five tasks, each its own landing
decisions.summary: Five changes (claims fail-fast, docstring-blind code id, cohort modes, make probe, task-add template), each landed separately; the cache key through make land
decisions.why: Exactly the GM's approval: the first 3 proposed fixes plus the cache key and cohort modes, plus the docstring audit.

decisions.id: Technical Context: single-artifact target and storage
decisions.summary: Key change proven first on the reference roll (Inashiro seed 4); probe baselines under .git/probe-baselines (untracked)
decisions.why: Verification of FR-003/SC-001 and the store FR-009 requires; adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Measure rolled/served counts before and after on a docs-only edit; baseline cohort-landing 54/54 and byte-identical manifests; cache-audit green
decisions.why: Measurement of SC-001 and the no-regression rule; verification of what was asked.

decisions.id: D1a - owed claim with nothing in flight returns at once; in-flight marker
decisions.summary: An owed claim with no live claims-in-flight marker ends the wait at once; claims-bundle/claims-triage write the marker, claims-checked/claims-triaged remove it, stale past CLAIMS_WAIT_S; while a live marker exists the landing waits as today; each message names its cure
decisions.why: FR-001/SC-002 (nothing in flight never enters the wait) and FR-002 (wait while in flight); the marker is the means of seeing 'in flight'. Fixes the earlier text, under which every owed refusal waited.

decisions.id: D1b - mixed refusal returns at once even with a check in flight
decisions.summary: When ANY part of the refusal is one waiting cannot cure, the wait ends at once even if an owed claim is also in flight
decisions.why: Literally departs from FR-002 (wait while a check is in flight). The GM's own words cover it: 'stop waiting when the claims gate refuses for a reason waiting can't fix' - a mixed refusal has such a reason, and waiting cannot end in a landing; the in-flight check's result is read by the next make land, so nothing is lost.

decisions.id: D2 - one shared docstring-blind code id
decisions.summary: New codeid module holding gate-stamp's existing normalization (drop docstrings, dump AST without attributes, hash); gate-stamp calls it; unparseable files hashed by bytes
decisions.why: FR-003/FR-004: one rule for every site the audit changes; the unparseable fallback keeps the cache exact (SC-006).

decisions.id: D3 - roll and render keys on codeid
decisions.summary: gencache._split_sources and render_cache.engine_fingerprint key .py on codeid
decisions.why: FR-003 and FR-005 as written.

decisions.id: D3 carve-out - interactive/** hashed raw in gencache and render_cache
decisions.summary: Files whose docstrings are an artifact's content (the class registry's docstrings are modal text via cls.__doc__; the page writer's text) keep byte hashing, reason recorded at the point of change
decisions.why: FR-004's 'unless a docstring is content of what it produces' and the GM's 'when we should': stripping these would serve a stale page whose text changed - the cache would stop being exact.

decisions.summary: Already docstring-blind; gate-stamp's normalization moves to codeid, RAW_AREAS stay raw
decisions.why: Already do what FR-004 asks; RAW_AREAS is the same content carve-out as D3.

decisions.summary: ci/state.py tooling_hash keys .py on codeid; function and class docstrings dropped (research R3: no tooling test reads __doc__/getdoc)
decisions.why: FR-004: a site failing to strip docstrings where it should; the GM's 'any other places'.

decisions.summary: Each .py file's module docstring stays in the key
decisions.why: Content of what the tooling produces: scripts print it as usage (regen.py, building_programs.py named). FR-004's content exception. The supporting clause 'a tooling test may assert on it' is hedged and unmeasured and is not relied on.

decisions.summary: The Makefile's ## help lines stay in the key
decisions.why: Content: they build docs/make-targets.html, so a change to them changes an output; FR-004's content exception.

decisions.id: Audit: tooling_hash Makefile plain '#' comments raw
decisions.summary: Non-.py files, the Makefile's ordinary comments included, stay hashed by bytes
decisions.why: Narrows the spec's 'comments' in FR-004, but against the request as written: the GM's words name docstrings ('failing to strip docstrings when we should'), and a Makefile has none; the reason is to be written at the point of change.

decisions.id: Audit: gate_config config_hash .py on codeid, lockfiles/config raw
decisions.summary: conftest and machinery on codeid; lockfiles and config files by bytes
decisions.why: FR-004 on the .py; lockfiles and config carry no docstrings.

decisions.summary: Extractor code keyed docstring-blind
decisions.why: FR-004: an extractor's docstring does not change what it extracts.

decisions.summary: The record's built site keeps byte hashing
decisions.why: Content: the build reads the engine's research claims, which live in docstrings; FR-004's exception.

decisions.summary: tools/claims.py and scripts/record/claims*.py fingerprints unchanged
decisions.why: Content: the claim text is the thing checked, so a docstring-blind key would let a changed claim skip its check; FR-004's exception.

decisions.id: Audit: plan/hook/record text hashes not touched
decisions.summary: plan blocks, transcripts, record pages are text hashes, not code-staleness keys
decisions.why: Outside FR-004's 'code-hashing site that decides whether work is stale'.

decisions.id: D4 - FAILED_FIRST / LAST_FAILED / EXITFIRST and the last run
decisions.summary: Three flags; 'last run' is the newest dev/cohort-log record of this clone with the same seed block; none: say so and roll all
decisions.why: FR-007 as written (the cohort's own records for the same seed block) and the GM's pytest-style modes.

decisions.id: D4 - EXITFIRST waits for rolls already started
decisions.summary: On the first failing result it cancels unstarted rolls, waits for started ones, reports the count left unrolled, exits 1
decisions.why: Up to pool-width seeds past the failure still finish, against 'without running the others' and SC-003's 'only'. On purpose grounds: those rolls are already running, the wait is bounded by one roll, and their results are stored and served next run; killing them would discard that work and force the re-roll the GM asked to stop.

decisions.id: D4 - partial records refused as a landing
decisions.summary: A --last-failed/--exitfirst record is marked partial and cohort_gate.landing_shaped refuses it; cohort-landing passes none of the flags
decisions.why: FR-008: the landing judges every seed.

decisions.id: D4 - rolled/served count and the FR-012 test through the landing path
decisions.summary: Every run prints 'rolled N, served M'; a test runs a full make cohort then make cohort-landing at the same code (and from a linked worktree) and asserts zero rolled
decisions.why: Measurement for SC-001 and the test FR-012 asks for; enforcement of what was asked. Now goes through the landing's own recipe, as FR-012 says.

decisions.summary: A partial run's failed list is its own failures plus the previous record's failures it did not roll
decisions.why: The pytest last-failed behavior the GM named ('do the pytest thing').

decisions.summary: Rolls the landing cohort, HEAD's fresh block and make map per live hamlet in WT; HEAD's verdicts stored per engine key and block, rolled once in a detached worktree when absent; prints EVERY seed's verdict beside HEAD's with the difference marked and each changed manifest field; EXITFIRST against the baseline
decisions.why: Fix 2 verbatim ('print each seed's result and each changed field against HEAD, with HEAD's results for a block stored once') and FR-009, SC-004. Fixes the earlier text, which printed only seeds that differed.

decisions.summary: New sections carry the alone-off table header and item 6's D35 red exit; a SECTION= lacking make arbiter-ask gets a warning and is filed
decisions.why: Fix 3 and FR-010 (MUST warn) as written.
